title: GET /api/analytics/exports lists every caller's exports with their files inline, and any signed-in user can request users and revenue exports: no role, tenant or user is used (KS-1703 covers only the by-id read)
description:
**BLUF:** `GET /api/analytics/exports` returns every analytics export the service holds, whoever asked for it, and a completed export carries its file inline (`downloadUrl` is a `data:` URI), so one list call returns other callers' files; and any signed-in caller can request the `users` and `revenue` report types, because the analytics service checks no role. KS-1703 already covers the by-id read (`GET /api/analytics/exports/{id}`, found by Schemathesis) and records that for exports "it may be deliberate" and needs a ruling; this ticket adds the list route, the missing role check on creation, and a rule the docs state that the code does not meet. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2, `WORKFLOWS.md` section 3). Related: KS-1703.

## What is not in KS-1703

* **The list route:** `router.get('/exports')` in `services/analytics/src/routes/analytics.ts` calls `exportService.listExports(limit)` (default 20), which returns the values of the service's process-wide map (`memExports` in `services/analytics/src/services/exportService.ts`) with no caller or tenant filter. KS-1703's table names the by-id read only. The list makes ids discoverable, so the by-id read does not even need a guessed id.
* **Creation has no role check and stores no caller:** `router.post('/exports')` parses the body and calls `exportService.createExport(request)`; the request carries no identity and `createExport` stores none. Accepted report types: `certifications`, `verifications`, `users`, `governance`, `revenue`, each built from `analyticsService.get<Type>Metrics(query)` where `query` holds only `period`, `startDate` and `endDate`. The gateway mount `/api/analytics` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts`) is `authenticateToken(true)` and the service mounts only `jwtAuthenticate` (`services/analytics/src/index.ts`): no role, no scope.
* **Persistence:** the newest 500 export rows are reloaded into the map at boot, so the exposure survives a restart.
* **Tenancy:** the word `tenant` appears in the analytics service's non-test source only in `db.ts`; the routes and `exportService.ts` never read a tenant or user from the request (control: the same search finds `req.params` in the routes file).

## A rule the docs state that this contradicts

`docs/security/ROLES-AND-AUTHORIZATION-INVENTORY.md` section 2.1 (as rewritten in KS-1807 PR-1) says services without a role gate "rely on gateway-level auth plus ownership and tenant checks"; for the analytics exports neither exists. PR-1 lists five routes as exceptions; this is a sixth, and PR-1's text will need one more name once this is ruled.

## How to confirm

As two users in different tenants: user A creates a `revenue` export and waits for `completed`; user B calls `GET /api/analytics/exports`. Expected by the platform's tenancy rule: B sees nothing of A's. By this reading: B receives A's export including the file. Not run. Not assessed: whether the metrics functions return platform-wide totals or are narrowed by a database tenant setting that this reading did not find.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves, and KS-1703 holds the open question whether exports are meant to be shared. If they are not: store the creating principal and tenant with each export, filter the list and the by-id read the same way and answer 404 to anyone else (as KS-1116 did for credentials), and decide which roles may request `users` and `revenue`.

Searched the board before filing: `analytics exports`, `listExports`, `exportService` and `analytics/exports` returned KS-1703 (by-id read, referenced above), KS-1853 and KS-1846 (this pass's tickets, about the export contract and the scope table) and KS-188 (stateful testing); none covers the list route or the missing role check. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: The gateway answers four admin and verify routes from stand-ins registered before the proxy: fixed audit-log arrays, an always-empty verification queue, and certification verify that always says verified:false
description:
**BLUF:** The api-gateway answers four routes itself, from stand-ins registered before the proxy to the real service, with no environment guard around them: `GET /api/admin/audit-logs` and `GET /api/security/audit` return fixed arrays of fabricated rows (actor `admin` at `test.local`), `GET /api/admin/verification-queue` returns an array nothing ever writes to (so it is always empty) and its action route answers `success: true` for any id without changing anything, and `POST /api/certifications/{id}/verify` always answers `verified: false` with a hard-coded issuer `test-issuer`. The real database-backed handlers in originate are never reached for the first three. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2, document lifecycle, status codes, error envelope). The docs and the published spec describe these as real operations; the code comment on the queue says "in-memory, development only" but nothing enforces that.

## Evidence

* **Registration order:** `app.use(createAdminRoutes(...))` and `app.use(createVerificationRoutes(...))` in `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` come before `app.use(createProxyRoutes(...))`, so a route defined in `routes/admin.ts` or `routes/verification.ts` answers before the `/api/admin/` proxy to originate is reached. The only environment check in `routes/admin.ts` is the demo-seed flag; none wraps these handlers.
* **Audit logs:** `router.get('/api/admin/audit-logs', requireAdmin, ...)` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` filters a literal 4-row array (`evt-1` to `evt-4`, actor `admin` at `test.local`) by `action` and `resourceType` and returns `{ success, logs, events, total }`. `router.get('/api/security/audit', ...)` does the same with a literal 3-row array. Originate has the real handler (`adminConfigRouter.get('/audit-logs')` in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`); it is shadowed.
* **Verification queue:** `const mockVerificationQueue = []` ("in-memory, development only") backs `GET /api/admin/verification-queue` (always `items: []`, `total: 0`) and `POST /api/admin/verification-queue/{id}/action`, which validates the action word, updates the array entry only if one exists, and answers `{ success: true, id, action, ... }` for any id. Originate's database-backed `GET`/`POST` for the same paths (`adminConfig.ts`) are shadowed.
* **Certification verify:** `router.post('/api/certifications/:id/verify', ...)` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` ("MOCK ... ENDPOINTS (for E2E tests)", "for test compatibility") checks that the certification exists, then answers `verified: false`, `status: 'issued'`, `issuer: { id: 'test-issuer', verified: true }`, `blockchain.anchored: false`, `confidence: 'pending-onchain'` whatever the certification is. Its comment says it is a stopgap "until the originate→anchoring rewire lands". Originate's own verify handler is never reached.
* **What the docs and spec say:** `QUICK-REFERENCE.md` lists all four as working endpoints (certification verify, the verification queue and its action, audit logs and the `security/audit` alias). The published spec declares only `GET /api/security/audit`; certification verify, `admin/audit-logs` and the two queue routes are live routes with no spec entry (0 hits for each path in `secuura-api.yaml`; control: `/api/billing/customers/by-email` hits).

## How to confirm

As a platform admin, call `GET /api/admin/audit-logs` on a stack with real audit rows and compare with the database; call the verification-queue action with a random id and read `success: true`; call certification verify on a real certification. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. Either remove the gateway stand-ins so the proxy reaches originate, or gate them to test environments behind an explicit flag and document that they are test doubles.

Searched the board before filing: `verification-queue` and `audit-logs` are not covered by an existing ticket about the gateway stand-ins; KS-736 is about mount authentication, not these handlers. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: Reset-password has no rate limit of its own (the limiter is mounted on /api/auth/password-reset, which has no route) and billing GET /customers/by-email can never match (/customers/:id is registered first)
description:
**BLUF:** Two routing slips in code that the docs describe as working: `POST /api/auth/reset-password`, the route that consumes a reset token, has no rate limit of its own because the reset limiter is mounted on `/api/auth/password-reset`, a path no route serves; and billing `GET /customers/by-email` can never match because `GET /customers/:id` is registered first and takes `by-email` as an id. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2). `WORKFLOWS.md`'s rate-limit sheet lists `password_reset` as 15 minutes, 5 attempts, on `POST /api/auth/password-reset`; the published spec declares `GET /api/billing/customers/by-email`.

## 1. The reset limiter guards a path with no handler

* **Limiter mounts** in `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` (`app.use(...)`, in this order): `/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/register`, `/api/auth/forgot-password` (1 hour, 5 in production, `PASSWORD_RESET_RATE_LIMIT`), `/api/auth/refresh`, `/api/auth/password-reset` (15 minutes, 5 in production, 50 otherwise), `/api/auth/verify-email`.
* **Auth routes** in `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` for the same flow: `POST /forgot-password` and `POST /reset-password`. There is no `/password-reset` route (control: the `/login` route is found by the same search).
* So `/api/auth/forgot-password` is limited, and `/api/auth/reset-password`, which takes the token and a new password, is limited only by the global limiter (300 per 60 s per IP in production). The 15-minute limiter on the dead path never sees a request. Not assessed: how guessable a reset token is; not probed.
* The login brute-force guard has a related defect already on the board: KS-1372 (nothing calls `recordFailure`).

## 2. Billing by-email is unreachable

`services/billing/src/routes/billing.ts` registers `router.get('/customers/:id', ...)` before `router.get('/customers/by-email', ...)`, so Express matches `by-email` as an `:id` and the by-email handler is never reached. The published spec declares `GET /api/billing/customers/by-email`.

## Not a finding (recorded in the PR for KS-1807 PR-2 as a doc correction)

`GET /billing/pricing` needs a login although a code comment calls it public: `services/billing/src/index.ts` says the public marketing endpoints are "intentionally behind JWT" (`app.use('/billing', jwtAuthenticate())`), so the doc is what is wrong.

Searched the board before filing: `password-reset`, `reset-password` and `by-email` returned no ticket about these two slips. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. Mount the limiter on `/api/auth/reset-password` (and drop or fix the dead mount), and register `/customers/by-email` before `/customers/:id`.

title: Spec and docs describe contracts the code does not follow: analytics export sends no Location or Retry-After and returns a data URI; kyc/submit and kyc/status are listed but absent; KYC approval never raises a verification level
description:
**BLUF:** In three areas the published spec and the docs describe a contract the code does not follow: the analytics export, the KYC steps, and the link between KYC and a user's verification level. The analytics export 202 declares `Location` and `Retry-After` headers and a poll-until-`done` flow; the code sends neither header, returns the file inline as a `data:` URI, and calls the field `downloadUrl`, not `url`. The spec's `info.x-workflows` lists `POST /api/kyc/submit` and `GET /api/kyc/status`, which do not exist. And no code path raises a user's verification level when a KYC verification is approved, although `WORKFLOWS.md` says it does. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2). The contract is generated from `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`, so correcting it is a product-source change and is held (findings only this round); this ticket is where it is decided which side moves.

## Analytics export (`services/analytics`)

* **Headers:** the spec's `POST /api/analytics/exports` 202 says "poll the URL in the `Location` header until state=`done`" and declares `Location` and `Retry-After` response headers. `services/analytics/src/routes/analytics.ts` sets no header (zero hits for `setHeader`, `res.set`, `location` or `retry-after`; control: `setHeader('Location'` has hits in originate's `documents.ts`).
* **Status values and fields:** `exportService.ts` sets `pending`, `processing`, `completed` and `failed`; the spec's `AnalyticsExport` schema has `completed` in its status enum but also declares `url`, `sizeBytes` and `completedAt`, which the code does not send. The code sends `downloadUrl` and `expiresAt`. `WORKFLOWS.md` says `ready` and `url` (a presigned URL with a finite TTL).
* **The download:** `downloadUrl` is `data:<mime>;base64,<payload>` (`createDownloadUrl` in `exportService.ts`), so the file travels inside the status response; there is no separate download request. `pdf` and `xlsx` exports contain JSON text, and `pdf` is labelled `application/octet-stream` (a placeholder, per its own comment).
* **Request and 202 body:** the spec's request declares `from` and `to`; the code reads `period` (required) with `startDate` and `endDate`, and also accepts `xlsx`. The 202 body is `{ success, data: { id, status, type, format, createdAt } }`, not the bare object.

## KYC (`services/kyc`)

* **Steps:** the spec's `info.x-workflows` lists `POST /api/kyc/submit` and `GET /api/kyc/status`. `services/kyc/src/index.ts` registers `initiate`, `/:id`, `/user/:userId`, `/:id/document`, `/:id/selfie`, `/:id/complete`, `/:id/review`, `/:id/result` and `DELETE /user/:userId/data`. `GET /api/kyc/status` is read as `/:id` with id `status` and answers 404; `POST /api/kyc/submit` matches no service route (by reading the gateway's method map it would answer 405, because the path matches the spec's `/api/kyc/{id}`, which allows only GET; not executed). `initiate` answers 201 (not 202) with `verificationId`; statuses are lowercase `pending`, `in_progress`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`.
* **The level never moves:** `WORKFLOWS.md` says `GET /api/users/me` shows the new `verificationLevel` after KYC and that a raised level unlocks higher-tier document types. A search of service source (tests excluded) finds `users.verification_level` written only by the gateway admin route, the social-login path in auth and originate's admin route; the kyc service has no access to the users table (0 hits for `FROM users`, `UPDATE users`, `INTO users` in `services/kyc/src`; control: `verification_level` has 5 hits in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`). So an approved KYC verification does not change a token's level by this reading. The seeded `PROPERTY_DEED` document type also needs no level (`creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'`), though the gate itself exists.

## Not repeated here

The create-document response shape (flat, not `DocumentDetail`), the `/anchor` 202 body, the verify `source` values and the error messages are recorded in the PR-2 pull request body as doc corrections, because there the code is plainly the intended behaviour; if you want them in the contract-corrections batch, say so.

Searched the board before filing: `kyc/submit`, `analytics exports`, `Retry-After` returned no ticket about these contract differences (KS-1327 is about KYC write races, KS-1372 about the login lockout). Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. For the export, either send the headers and a real download, or change the spec and docs to the inline `data:` form; for KYC, remove the two steps from `x-workflows` and decide whether approval should raise the level.

title: api-gateway: a 401 or 403 from in front of the security service is cached as a 30 s key rejection; should an infrastructure 401/403 count as "could not answer"? (gate 31, F2)
description:
**BLUF:** A design question, not a defect found today. The gateway's `checkApiKey` treats any non-OK status from the key-validate call outside 5xx, 408 and 429 as a key rejection and negative-caches it for about 30 s (answering 401 `Invalid API key`). By the gate's reading, the real `/api/keys/validate` never answers 401 or 403 (`security/src/index.ts:775-779` skips JWT auth for that path; the handler near line 1800 answers 400, 503 or 200 with `valid: false`), so a 401 or 403 at the gateway would come from something **in front of** the security service (ingress or a WAF) and would make every key, valid ones included, answer 401 `Invalid API key` for 30 s. Pull request 1827 (KS-1788 item 3) now pins today's behaviour for a 403, which turns it into a tested contract. Should an infrastructure 401/403 count as "could not answer" (503, not cached) instead?

**Source.** QA gate 31 on pull request 1827 (KS-1788 item 3; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-30), finding F2 (Note, a design question for Kam, not that pull request's defect). Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate31-1827/verdict.md`. Related: KS-1788, where the 403 cell was asked for; KS-1174, which is about forwarding a distinct code per key failure and not about this classification; KS-1240, the original timeout work. Filed on Wednesday's word.

**The verdict text, quoted (F2, lines 56 to 59 of the verdict, unedited):**

* **F2 (Note, design question for Kam, not this PR's defect).** The cell freezes "any non-OK status outside {5xx, 408, 429} is a key rejection, negative-cached 30 s".
  * The real `/api/keys/validate` never answers 401 or 403. `security/src/index.ts:775-779` skips JWT auth for that path, and the handler at l.1800 answers 400 (schema), 503 (KS-1370) or 200 `valid:false`.
  * So a 401 or 403 at the gateway would come from something **in front of** the security service (ingress or WAF). Today that would answer every key, valid ones included, `401 Invalid API key` for 30 s.
  * Pinning today's behaviour is what the ticket asked for, so this is fine to merge. But this PR now makes it a pinned contract, so whether an infrastructure 401/403 should count as "could not answer" deserves a ruling.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `checkApiKey` 1 hit (KS-1788). `couldNotAnswer` 0, `infrastructure 401` 0, `negative cache` 2 (KS-1788, KS-1207: neither asks this), `keys/validate` 23 (read: KS-1174, KS-1788, KS-1240 for ingress, WAF, status or "could not answer" text: none asks whether an infrastructure 401/403 is a rejection), `WAF` 8 (none about the key-validate call).

**Not measured by this filing:** the security service's routes (the statements about them are the gate's reading, not re-read here); what any ingress or WAF in front of the service answers in practice; whether one exists on any box.

title: vc-issuer POST /api/credentials/{id}/revoke checks neither owner nor role: any signed-in caller can revoke any credential by id (the KS-1116 binding covers reads only)
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/credentials/{id}/revoke` in vc-issuer checks neither the caller's role nor who created the credential. Any signed-in caller who knows a credential id can revoke it. KS-1116 bound the credential and presentation READS to the creating principal; the revoke write was left out. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1, authentication, roles and scopes). Filed on the coordinator's word (2026-10-30 ANSWER, 01:40Z). Related: KS-1116 (the creator binding, reads only) and KS-1845 (admin or owner checks missing on routes that need them).

## Evidence

* **Route:** `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts`, `router.post('/:id/revoke', ...)`: takes `id` from the path and an optional `reason` from the body, calls `credentialRepo.revoke(id, reason)`, answers 404 "Credential not found" when it returns nothing, otherwise 200 with `credentialId` and `revokedAt`. There is no role check and no comparison with the credential's creator.
* **Repository:** `services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`, `revoke()`: looks the credential up with `getById(id)` (the exact-id lookup that KS-1116 deliberately left unbound for the public verify path), rewrites its `credentialStatus` (`revoked: true`, `revokedAt`, `revocationReason`) in the in-memory store, and runs `UPDATE vc_credentials_store SET credential = $1 WHERE id = $2`. The SQL has no owner or tenant condition. Not checked: whether row-level security on that table limits the update to the caller's tenant.
* **What sits in front:** the gateway mount `/api/credentials` is `authenticateToken(false)`; the service's own `jwtAuthenticate` on `/api` requires a valid token for everything except its three public operations (verify credential, verify presentation, the identity-credential types), so an anonymous caller is refused. Any valid token passes, whatever its role or tenant.
* **The binding that exists:** `services/vc-issuer/src/ownership.ts` (`mayRead`) binds `GET /api/credentials/{id}`, the credential list and the by-hash read (KS-1683) to the creating principal; its header names only the public verify path's revocation lookup as deliberately unbound and does not mention revoke. `ks1116-presentation-and-credential-reads-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts` exercises revoke only by the creator.
* **Why it matters:** the public verify path's revocation lookup reads the stored revoked status (`credentialStatus.revoked`), so this is a write that changes another principal's credential into a revoked one. Not assessed: how guessable a credential id is, and whether the verify routes act on the flag (KS-1352 and KS-1375 are about exactly that).

## How to confirm

Create a credential as user A, revoke it by id with a token for user B in the same tenant (and one in another tenant). Expected by the KS-1116 ruling's intent: 404 or 403. By this reading: 200. Not run.

## What the docs say

`docs/security/ROLES-AND-AUTHORIZATION-INVENTORY.md` (KS-1807 PR-1) records the gap as a fact with an `UNDECIDED (KS-1807, 2026-10-30)` line, because the KS-1116 ruling covers reads and no ruling says who may revoke.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. The shape of the existing binding would extend naturally: read the owner with `getRecordById`, apply `mayRead` (or a revoke variant that also admits the tenant administrators), and answer a refused caller exactly like an unknown id.

Searched the board before filing: `credentials/{id}/revoke`, `credential revoke`, `credentialRepo.revoke` and `revoke a credential` returned KS-188, KS-1352, KS-1375, KS-1684 and KS-692 and none is about the missing owner or role check on this route (KS-1352 and KS-1375: a revoked credential still verifies; KS-1684: the creator refused a read after a revoke on the memory path; KS-692: the status revoke route's tenant check; KS-1116 and KS-1683 are about reads). Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: Two admin routes admit OWNER, the self-registration default: billing POST /admin/credits and nft-certificate PUT /admin/platform-fee answer 403 "Admin access required" but let any registered user through
description:
**BLUF:** Two routes that answer 403 "Admin access required" let `OWNER` through. `OWNER` is the role every self-registered user gets (registration always assigns it), so any registered user passes both: `POST /admin/credits` in `services/billing/src/routes/billing.ts`, which adds certification credits to a customer (credits are money), and `PUT /admin/platform-fee` in `services/nft-certificate/src/routes/nft.routes.ts`, which sets the NFT platform fee. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1, authentication, roles and scopes). Filed on the coordinator's word (2026-10-30 ANSWER, 01:40Z). Related: KS-1845 (the same class: admin-labelled routes with no or too wide a role gate).

## The routes

1. **billing** `POST /admin/credits` — comment "Add certification credits to a customer (admin only)". The handler reads `req.user?.role` and answers 403 `FORBIDDEN` "Admin access required" unless the role is in `['SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN', 'OWNER']`. It then parses `{ customerId: string, credits: positive integer }` and calls `getStripeService().addCertificationCredits(customerId, credits)`, answering `{ customerId, creditsAdded, newBalance }`. Nothing ties `customerId` to the caller's own account or organisation. The gateway mount `/api/billing` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` is `authenticateToken(false)` plus the proxy.
2. **nft-certificate** `PUT /api/nft/admin/platform-fee` — comment "Update platform fee configuration (admin only)". Same role list and the same 403 body. It then parses `{ percentage: 0-100, fixed: >= 0 }` and calls `costEstimatorService.updatePlatformFee(percentage, fixed)`, answering the new values. The gateway mount `/api/nft` is `authenticateToken(false)` plus a proxy guard.

`OWNER` is assigned on every registration path (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` sets `role: 'OWNER'`; an explicit `role` in the request is refused 422), so for these two routes "Admin access required" admits every registered user. A search of `services` and `packages` source (tests and docs excluded) for a bracketed list containing the string `'OWNER'` returns exactly these two lines; the control, the same pattern on the billing file alone, hits it.

## How to confirm

One request to each route with a token whose role is `OWNER` (a freshly registered user). Expected by the route's own message: 403. By this reading: 200 with the new balance, and 200 with the new fee. Not run.

## What the docs say

`docs/security/ROLES-AND-AUTHORIZATION-INVENTORY.md` (KS-1807 PR-1) records the two inline lists as a fact with an `UNDECIDED (KS-1807, 2026-10-30)` line, because no ruling says whether `OWNER` is meant to pass; this ticket is where that is decided.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. If "admin only" is the intent, drop `OWNER` from both lists (or use the shared `requireRole`) and, for credits, bind `customerId` to the caller's own customer unless the caller is a platform admin.

Searched the board before filing: `admin/credits` 0 hits, `platform-fee` 1 hit (KS-1820, about the NFT mint and the platform wallet, not these role lists). Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: auth backup-code cells: none pins what the burn writes, so burning the wrong code, writing the array back unchanged or deleting every code passes all 347 cells (gate 30, F2)
description:
**BLUF:** No backup-code cell in `services/auth` pins what the burn writes. Burning the wrong index, writing the array back unchanged, or deleting every code each pass all 347 backup-code cells. Test strength, pre-existing; no product defect is claimed by this ticket.

**Source.** QA gate 30 on pull request 1826 (KS-1804 note 2; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-30), finding F2 (Minor, test strength, pre-existing). Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate30-1826/verdict.md`. Related: KS-1804, KS-1052 (the class of updateUser callers that discard the return, which first put a burn under test) and KS-1848 (the non-atomic burn, finding F1 of the same gate). Filed on Wednesday's word.

**The verdict text, quoted (F2, lines 51 to 54 of the verdict, unedited):**

* **F2 (Minor, test strength, pre-existing).** No backup-code cell pins WHAT the burn writes.
  * Burning the wrong index, writing the array unchanged, or deleting every code (b1/b2/b3) all pass every one of the 347 cells.
  * The new healthy cell is titled "burns the code with exactly one UPDATE users" but asserts only the count. `ks781` LEG 4 ("authorizes AND is burned") asserts only that `updateUserOrThrow` was called.
  * **Suggested pin:** record the `values` in the db stub and assert that the written `mfa_backup_codes` equals the stored array minus the used hash.

The terms for the burn (`mfa_backup_codes`, `mfaBackupCodes`, `array_remove`, `backup code twice`, `burn is not atomic`) returned no ticket about what a burn writes; the hits and the neighbours read for it are listed on KS-1848.

title: auth: the single-use backup-code burn is not atomic (passwordLoginGate.ts:273-285, userRepo.ts:891-894), so concurrent sign-ins can reuse a spent code (gate 30, F1)
description:
**BLUF:** The single-use backup-code burn in the password-login gate is not atomic. It reads the stored code array, splices the used code out in memory and writes the whole array back matched by user id only (`passwordLoginGate.ts:273-285`, `userRepo.ts:891-894`). **Measured against a stateful stub, not against Postgres:** two concurrent sign-ins with the same code both get a credential, and two concurrent sign-ins with different codes can leave a spent code stored and accepted again (a lost update). Pre-existing; no current change introduces it.

**Source.** QA gate 30 on pull request 1826 (KS-1804 note 2; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-30), finding F1 (Major, pre-existing product, out of that pull request's scope; the gate recommends filing). Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate30-1826/verdict.md`; the probe `g30-probe-race.test.ts` (P1 and P2) sits beside it. Related: KS-1804, where it was found, and the neighbours the gate named, KS-809, KS-1052 and KS-1081, none of which is about concurrency. KS-1327 is the same whole-row read-modify-write class on KYC writes, not on backup codes. Filed on Wednesday's word.

**The verdict text, quoted (F1, lines 46 to 50 of the verdict, unedited):**

* **F1 (Major, PRE-EXISTING product, out of this PR's scope; recommend filing).** The single-use burn is not atomic.
  * **Where:** `passwordLoginGate.ts:273-285` + `userRepo.ts:891-894`. The code reads, then splices in memory, then writes the whole array by `WHERE id` only.
  * **Effect:** two concurrent logins with one backup code both get a credential, and two concurrent logins with different codes can leave a spent code valid (a lost update). Measured against a stateful stub (probe P1 and P2), NOT against Postgres.
  * **Board search (Linear** `searchIssues`**, includeArchived):** no ticket matched literally on "backup code concurrent", "backup code race", "mfa_backup_codes race" or "backup code twice"; the fuzzy hits were KS-809, KS-1052 and KS-1081, none about concurrency. Control: a nonsense term gave 0. KS-1052 and KS-533 contain no race or concurrency text (grep).
  * **Possible remedies (not built):** `UPDATE … SET mfa_backup_codes = array_remove(mfa_backup_codes, $hash) WHERE id = $id AND $hash = ANY(mfa_backup_codes)`, requiring rowCount 1; or `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` in a transaction.

**Fix shape (the gate's, not built here):** a conditional update that removes exactly the presented code and requires it to be present, or a row lock, as quoted above. It touches the credential path, so the fix would get a tier-1 gate.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `passwordLoginGate` 13 hits including KS-1804. `mfa_backup_codes` 5 hits (KS-1052, KS-938, KS-809, KS-795, KS-783), `mfaBackupCodes` 6 (KS-938, KS-809, KS-783, KS-732, KS-622, KS-256), `array_remove` 0, `backup code race` 0, `backup code twice` 0, `burn is not atomic` 0, `lost update` 4 (KS-1377, KS-1370, KS-772, KS-485: none about backup codes), `FOR UPDATE` 2 (KS-1327, KS-757: neither about backup codes). KS-809, KS-1052, KS-1081, KS-533 and KS-1804 read whole for race or concurrency text: no statement about concurrent burns.

**Not measured by this filing:** anything against Postgres; both effects were shown against a stateful stub by the gate's probe, and this ticket does not repeat it.

title: Docs claim rules the code does not apply: share checks no document access, ownerless documents skip the read check, a revoked key works 60 s at the gateway, the admin dashboard reads X-Tenant-Override, metering is certification-only
description:
**BLUF:** Five statements in the platform-k security docs describe a rule the code does not apply: document share checks no per-document access, a document with no recorded owner skips the read check, a revoked API key is still accepted by the gateway for up to 60 seconds, `GET /api/admin/dashboard` reads `X-Tenant-Override` from the raw header for an `ORG_ADMIN`, and the claim that agent document operations are metered holds only for certification operations. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; none of these was exercised against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1). The docs and the code disagree on each; PR-1 describes what is built, names this ticket beside the passage, and does not write either behaviour as the intended one.

## Items

1. **Share has no per-document access check.** `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`): after the role-or-scope gate (`DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` or `documents:share`) the handler runs `getDocument(id, tenantId)` and answers 404 only when the document is absent from the tenant; it never compares the caller with the owner, a recipient or an admin. `AGENT-DOCUMENT-OPERATION-RULES.md` R4 says "ownership checks still apply on read/share/revoke". Same class as KS-1688 (version) and KS-1814 (anchor; fixed), and as KS-1833/KS-1834 (lifecycle events).
2. **Ownerless documents skip the read check.** `GET /api/documents/{id}`: the refusal is guarded by `userId && document.owner?.id && document.owner.id !== userId && !isAdmin && !isRecipient`. `documentRepo` maps the owner as `row.owner_user_id || row.issuer_user_id || ''`, so a row with neither column set has `owner.id === ''` and the guard is false for every caller in the tenant. The inventory (§2.3) says reading needs owner, admin, recipient or creating connector. Not measured: how many rows have no owner.
3. **A revoked key keeps working at the gateway.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts` caches a valid `sk_` key in `apiKeyCache` for 60 s (a rejection for 30 s); nothing outside tests deletes or clears the cache (zero hits for `apiKeyCache.delete` and `apiKeyCache.clear`; control: `apiKeyCache.set` has two). The security service's revoke is immediate. The rules doc R6 says keys are "revocable immediately", contract §5 says "takes effect on next validate", and the rotation grace default `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS=0` was ruled "instant revoke" (2026-08-07, KS-577).
4. `X-Tenant-Override` **is read raw by one admin route.** The inventory (§2.4) says the override is "honoured only for the super-admin list". The gateway applies that list when it sets the tenant GUC, but it also allow-lists the header through to the services (`TRUST_HEADER_ALLOW_LIST` in `services/api-gateway/src/utils/trustHeaders.ts`), and `GET /api/admin/dashboard` in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts` reads `req.headers['x-tenant-override']` itself and, if it is a UUID, counts documents, users and verifications for that tenant under `runWithPlatformScope`; with no header it returns platform-wide totals. That router admits `ORG_ADMIN` (`requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN')`) and so does the gateway's `/api/admin/` proxy (`enforceAdminProxy`). By this reading an `ORG_ADMIN` can read counts for another tenant. Counts only; not exercised live.
5. **Metering covers certifications only.** The rules doc R7 says agent document operations are metered (KS-320). `charge_events` rows are inserted only by `services/originate/src/services/chargeEvents.ts`, which only `routes/certifications.ts` calls for writes; `documents.ts` and anchoring do not import it. Create, version, share, revoke, transfer-custody and anchor write none. Which operations should be metered is a product call, not a code reading.

Related and not repeated: KS-1433 (connectors cannot revoke; unenforced scopes), KS-1688, KS-1833, KS-1834, KS-1814.

Searched the board before filing: `x-tenant-override` 8 hits (none about the dashboard; KS-1704 is about a super-admin's override), `apiKeyCache` 0, `charge_events` 1 (KS-1401, RLS on the table, not coverage), `lifecycle-events` hits KS-1833 and KS-1834 (excluded above). Controls in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns. Items 1 and 2 are access checks in originate; item 3 is a cache invalidation or a stated TTL; item 4 is to read the override from the verified request context, not the header; item 5 needs a ruling on what is metered first.

title: Scope vocabulary and enforcement drift: five scopes gate nothing or name missing routes, gateway requireScope ignores <resource>:*, mints never call validateScopes, * is mintable by every key-admin role (SCOPES.md vs code)
description:
**BLUF:** Six differences between what `SCOPES.md` (and the KS-540 inventory) say about scopes and what the code enforces. Five scopes in the vocabulary gate nothing or name routes that do not exist; the gateway's `requireScope` does not honour `<resource>:*` although the shared helper does; the key mints never call `validateScopes`; `*` can be minted by every key-admin role although the docs say super-admin only; and gates and mints use scope strings that are not in the 32-member `SCOPES` array. `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke` (minted but unenforced) are already tracked in KS-1433 and are not repeated here. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; the gateway and mint behaviour was not exercised against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1). PR-1 rewrites `SCOPES.md` to describe what is built and marks each open question `UNDECIDED (KS-1807, 2026-10-30)`; this ticket is where the code side is decided.

## Items

1. **Declared, enforced nowhere.** `certifications:share`: `POST /api/certifications/{id}/share` exists in `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts` with no scope or role check (and is not in the published spec). `certifications:revoke`: the route checks the caller is the certification's issuer, no scope (not in the spec). `analytics:read`: the `/api/analytics` gateway mount is authentication only. `analytics:export`: `POST /api/analytics/exports` exists (in the spec) with no scope check. `users:write`: no reference in any source file outside `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts`.
2. **Names routes that do not exist.** `certifications:sign` (no `/{id}/sign` route in originate, not in the spec), `kyc:submit` (no `/api/kyc/submit`), `kyc:read` (no `/api/kyc/status`). The vocabulary entries are pinned by `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks843-subjects-erase-scope.test.ts`, so removing them is a decision and a test edit.
3. **Gateway wildcard.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/scopes.ts` `requireScope` tests `userScopes.includes(s)` (exact) plus a lone `*`; the imported shared `hasScope` is shadowed by a local `const hasScope` in the same function. A key holding only `documents:*` is refused 403 on `GET /api/documents` and every other `/api/documents` method except create (the gateway's create handler in `routes/verification.ts` does accept `documents:*`). The KS-843 comment in the same file already calls the exact match "silent". No gateway test covers a `<resource>:*` key (control: the shared tests have 8 such cells).
4. **No validation at mint.** `services/security/src/index.ts` mint schema is `scopes: z.array(z.string()).default(['read'])`; originate `POST /api/admin/api-keys` (`services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`) stores the list as given; the shared `validateScopes` has no caller outside its own tests. The default `read` is not a vocabulary scope.
5. `*` **is not reserved.** `decideMint` in `services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts` allows every `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` member (`SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ADMIN`) with any scope list, `*` included; only a provisioning key is refused wildcards. `SCOPES.md` says `*` is "reserved for super-admin keys".
6. **Out-of-vocabulary strings in use.** `webhooks:manage` (gates `/api/webhooks`), `users:create` (accepted by auth's `POST /api/users/stub`), `register` (legacy literal in the gateway's create handler), `metering:read` (minted onto the metering key by `services/tenant-provisioning/src/meteringKey.ts`; no gate reads it), `read`/`write` (mint defaults and the fixed set the admin portal sends), and the OAuth list (`verify:read`, `admin:read`, `admin:write` in `services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts`). The KS-540 inventory raised items 3, 4 and 6 as F-3, F-4 and F-5 on 2026-07-31; none is done.

Related and not repeated: KS-1433 (anchors:read, documents:revoke), KS-1777 (the flat 403 body of `requireScope`), KS-1653 (`certifications:write` admits `POST /api/users/stub`), KS-839 (OAuth `*`), KS-1535 and KS-1536 (which roles may mint keys).

Searched the board before filing: `certifications:share`, `certifications:revoke`, `analytics:read`, `users:write`, `kyc:submit`, `certifications:sign`, `metering:read` and `hasScope` each 0 hits; `wildcard` 4 hits (KS-839, KS-1584, KS-1156, KS-1210, none about the gateway helper); `validateScopes` 2 hits (KS-839, KS-1156). Controls in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843 and `documents:revoke` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 (docs lead, code aligns), either make each declared scope gate its route, or take the entry out of the vocabulary and out of the docs; make `requireScope` call `hasScope`; call `validateScopes` at both mints; restrict `*` to the roles the docs name. Which of these is intended is open, and PR-1 says so in the docs.

title: POST /api/kyc/:id/review has no role or owner check: any signed-in caller can approve a verification and set its level, though the spec declares 403 "Reviewer role required" (four more admin-labelled routes ungated)
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/kyc/:id/review` approves or rejects a KYC verification and sets its `currentLevel` (up to `GOVERNMENT`), but it checks no role and no ownership. The only authentication in front of it is `jwtAuthenticate` on `/api` inside the kyc service and `authenticateToken(true)` on the `/api/kyc` gateway mount, so any signed-in caller who knows the id of a verification in state `under_review` can decide it. The published spec declares `403 Reviewer role required` on this operation. Four more routes that their own comments or the spec call admin-only have the same shape. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; nothing was probed against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1, authentication, roles and scopes). Doc-versus-code difference: the spec (and the inventory's "they rely on gateway auth + ownership/tenant checks") says a gate exists; the code has none.

## The routes

1. **kyc review** — `services/kyc/src/index.ts`, handler for `POST /api/kyc/:id/review`. It parses `reviewVerificationSchema` (`status` approved or rejected, optional `reviewNotes`, optional `newLevel` NONE to GOVERNMENT), takes `reviewerId` from `req.user?.userId` (falling back to the string `admin`), then writes `verification.status` and, on approval, `verification.currentLevel = data.newLevel || verification.requestedLevel` and saves it. There is no `requireRole`, and nothing compares the verification's owner with the caller. Spec: `services/kyc/src/kyc.openapi.ts` declares the 403 with the description "Reviewer role required". Gateway: the `/api/kyc` mount in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` is `authenticateToken(true)` plus the proxy. Not checked: whether the verification's `currentLevel` is read back into a user's token level elsewhere.
2. **governance** — `POST /api/governance/process-expired` in `services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts` (comment: "admin/cron endpoint"); spec `governance.openapi.ts` declares 403 "Admin role required". The gateway mount `/api/governance` uses `authenticateToken(false)` (the shape KS-736 tracks).
3. **transfer** — `POST /api/delegations/admin/process-expired` in `services/transfer/src/routes/delegations.ts` (comment: "admin trigger"). Mount is authentication only.
4. **staking** — `GET /api/stake/all` in `services/staking/src/routes/stake.ts` (comment: "List all stakes (admin)"); the handler pages `SELECT * FROM svc_stake_positions`. Mount is authentication only. Not checked: whether that table is tenant-scoped.
5. **wallet-connector** — `GET /api/wallets/sessions` in `services/wallet-connector/src/server.ts` (comment: "List active sessions (admin)"). Mount is authentication only.

For all five the service mounts no role gate (a census of `services/*/src` for `requireRole`, role comparisons and `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` finds none in kyc, governance, transfer, staking or wallet-connector; the same census finds originate's 73 hits, so the instrument fires).

## Evidence and how to confirm

Read at `develop` `530f09112`. A live check is one request per route with a token whose role is `OWNER` (the self-registration default); the expected answer by the spec is 403, and by this reading it is 2xx (or 404 for an unknown id). Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Peter's ruling recorded on KS-1668: the docs lead and the code aligns to them; Kam decides which side moves. The aligned fix is a role gate on each route (the shared `requireRole` in `packages/shared/src/middleware/index.ts` is already mounted in billing, tokenisation and vc-issuer), and for the kyc review an owner-not-reviewer check as well. KS-1807's PR-1 documents the difference rather than the intended gate, and marks the passage so a test is not written against current behaviour.

Searched the board before filing: `Reviewer role required` 0 hits, `process-expired` 1 unrelated hit (KS-1762), `kyc/:id/review` 1 unrelated hit (KS-1327, a read-modify-write race). Control in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843.

title: certifications.ts GET /:id catch reads code, meta.code and message of the thrown value unguarded: a hostile throw gets no answer
description:
**BLUF:** The catch of originate `GET /api/certifications/:id` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts`: handler at :1020, catch at :1065, the unguarded reads at :1073 and :1074, develop `530f091120d5`) reads `code`, `meta.code` and `message` straight off the thrown value, and tests `error instanceof Error`, with no try of its own. A thrown value whose property read throws (a revoked Proxy, or a getter that throws) therefore throws inside the catch of an async Express 4 handler, and the request gets no answer. Same family as KS-1798 (the GDPR write routes, in review) and KS-1780 (Done: systemErrors, adminConfig, `extractPgCode`). Found while building KS-1798. Read, and probed at the language level; not run on this route.

**What I read**

* `certifications.ts:1020` is `GET /:id`, an `async` handler. Its `catch (error)` at :1065 runs `const pgCode = (error as { code?: string })?.code ?? (error as { meta?: { code?: string } })?.meta?.code;` (:1073), then `error instanceof Error && error.message.includes('22P02')` (:1074), then `logger.error(... error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error))` (:1077). None of the three is inside a try.
* The same file already does the safe thing elsewhere: :926 reads the code through `extractPgCode(error)`, which KS-1780 made safe against a hostile thrown value.
* Express in this tree is 4.22.3, which does not forward a rejected async handler promise, so a throw out of the catch block leaves the request unanswered. KS-1798's cells D1 and D2 show exactly that on the gdpr routes (a request with no answer in 1500 ms; 3 of 20 red before the guard). That is the measured mechanism; it was not run on this route.
* Language-level probe on Node v26.8.1: with a revoked Proxy, `error?.code` throws a TypeError and so does `error instanceof Error`; with an Error whose `code` getter throws, `error?.code` throws; an ordinary Error reads without throwing.
* A scan of non-test originate `src` for the pattern `(error as { code?` finds this site only (the other hit, `documentRepo.ts:903`, writes a code onto its own Error).

**Why it is not fixed here**

* `certifications.ts` is outside the pass that found it, and Wednesday ruled this is a separate lane (the file was changed by pull request 1822, merged at `530f091120d5`).
* Exposure is low: the value comes from `getCertification`, a database layer that raises Prisma and pg errors; a hostile value cannot be sent from outside (KS-1780 records the same). Priority 4.

**Suggested shape (not designed, not tested):** classify through `extractPgCode(error)`, put the `instanceof` and `message` reads behind one guarded helper, and add cells like KS-1798's D1 and D2 for this route.

**Searched** (whole-board census, 1832 issues of which 1009 archived, 5195 comments, local regex over title, description and comments; every hit read): `certifications\.ts:?\s*10[67][0-9]` 0 hits; `meta\??\.code` 3 hits (KS-1799, KS-1798, KS-1780: all about `extractPgCode` in `pgErrors.ts`, a different file); `certifications\.ts.{0,80}(meta|code)` 3 hits (KS-1666, a comment-only change to two comments in the same file; KS-1475 `certifications.ts:563` and KS-537 `certifications.ts:513/521`, both different defects); a random token 0 (not recorded here). No ticket covers this site.

**Not measured:** a reproduction on this route (no cell run); whether `getCertification` can throw a non-Error value at all; other originate catches that read a thrown value (KS-1780's own census was 17).

title: nft-certificate: the row-owner trim is asymmetric between the two read paths, and getWalletNFTCertificates still gets the raw ?walletAddress (gate 23, F2 and F3)
description:
**BLUF:** Two follow-ups from the gate on pull request 1819 (KS-1836), neither a regression. F2 (Low): `selectReadableCertificates` compares `cert.userId.trim()` with the owner, while `getUserNFTCertificates(ownerId)` matches `cert.userId === userId` exactly, so a row stamped `'user-A '` is returned to user-A on the `?walletAddress` path but not on the bare list. The trim never lets a different owner through; mutant Mc (drop the trim) survives every cell; no write path stamps a padded owner today. F3 (Info): `getWalletNFTCertificates` still receives the raw `?walletAddress` string (parameterised equality, no injection); removing that is a design choice, not a defect.

**Source.** QA gate 23 on pull request 1819 (KS-1836; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-29), findings F2 and F3 only. F1 of the same gate (the foreign-selector log arm) is being worked separately under KS-1836 and is not part of this filing. Related: KS-1836. Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate23-1819/verdict.md`.

**The verdict text, quoted (F2 and F3, lines 32 to 52 of the verdict, unedited):**

**F2 (Low, consistency). The row-owner trim is asymmetric between the two read paths.**

* **What happens:**
  * `selectReadableCertificates` compares `cert.userId.trim()` with the owner.
  * `getUserNFTCertificates(ownerId)` matches `cert.userId === userId` exactly, both in memory and in SQL.
  * So a row stamped `'user-A '` is returned to user-A on the `?walletAddress` path but not on the bare list. Attack cell A-M2 logged `padded-row/null-row -> ["n2"]`.
* **What does not happen:** the trim never lets a different owner through. It only matters for rows whose trimmed owner equals the caller.
* **Mutant:** Mc (drop the trim) survives every cell. No fixture has a padded owner.
* **Reachability:** no write path stamps a padded owner today; every row is `'user-id'`.

**F3 (Info). The wallet reader still receives attacker-controlled strings.**

* **What I saw:** `getWalletNFTCertificates` is called with the raw `?walletAddress` string, for example `" "`, `"%"` and `" addr_..."` (A-Q log lines).
* **No injection:** the query is parameterised equality (`wallet_address = $1`), not LIKE.
* **Side effects:**
  * The foreign wallet's rows are read and cached into `memNftCertificates`, which `loadFromDb` already fills at boot anyway.
  * In-process timing difference, a median of 15 calls:
    * foreign wallet with 0 rows: 1.59 ms;
    * foreign wallet with 2000 rows: 1.91 ms.
  * That is a weak size oracle at best. I measured it over loopback in-process, not over a network.
* **What would remove both:** querying by `ownerId` and narrowing by wallet in memory. That is a design choice, not a defect.
* The userId selector never reaches a service method. Every A-Q cell shows the user reader called only with `["user-A"]`.

**Where this lands.** Its own ticket and not a comment on KS-1836, because KS-1836 closes when a deploy round carries pull request 1819's merge, and these follow-ups outlive it. KS-1836 read whole: it holds neither F2 nor F3.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `getUserNFTCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836). `selectReadableCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836); `getWalletNFTCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836); `row-owner` 0; `userId.trim` 0; `padded` 20 hits, of which the first 15 titles were read and none is about the NFT read paths.

**Not measured by this filing:** nothing was run here; the timing figures in F3 are the gate's in-process loopback measurements.

title: api-gateway Dockerfile:35: the backup `rm -f` glob misses six name shapes, a backup-named directory fails the build, and the backups stay in the build context (gate 24, F1 to F3)
description: **BLUF:** The api-gateway Dockerfile line `RUN rm -f ./docs/openapi/*.pre-* ./docs/openapi/*.rollback-*` (`services/api-gateway/Dockerfile:35`, added by pull request 1820 for KS-1823) removes two backup-name shapes. Six other shapes still reach the final image (F1), the backups still enter the build context and the builder layer (F2), and a directory named like a backup fails the build (F3). Hygiene, not a stated exposure: the gate's runtime check found no reader of the backups (the only spec reader is `index.ts:590-605`, fixed path `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`). **Source.** QA gate 24 on pull request 1820 (tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-29), findings F1, F2 and F3 of its verdict. The two shapes that actually sit on the demo host are covered, so this is not a regression. Related: KS-1823. Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate24-1820/verdict.md`. **The verdict text, quoted (lines 32 to 66 of the verdict, unedited):** **F1 (Low, completeness). The glob removes two name shapes. Six other backup shapes still reach the image.** * **Where:** `services/api-gateway/Dockerfile:35`. * **What:** I planted these in `docs/openapi` in my clone and built with the head's Dockerfile. | Shape | Result | | -- | -- | | `x.pre-test` | REMOVED | | `x.rollback-test` | REMOVED | | `secuura-api.yaml.pre-ks508` (the real host shape) | REMOVED | | `secuura-api.yaml.rollback-2026-08-27-ks661` (the real host shape) | REMOVED | | `.z.pre-test` (a dotfile; busybox `*` does not match a leading dot) | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `secuura-api.yaml.PRE-upper` (the glob is case-sensitive) | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `sub/y.pre-test` (the glob covers the top level only) | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `x.bak` | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `x.orig` | **STILL IN IMAGE** | | `x~` | **STILL IN IMAGE** | * **Control:** all 10 shapes are present in the develop-Dockerfile image (`ls_develop_decoys.txt`). * **The .dockerignore does not cover any of them.** `Blockchain/Dev/.dockerignore` has `docs` then `!docs/openapi`, which re-includes the whole directory. Its `*.md` is root-only, which is why WORKFLOWS.md and TRACK2_OPENAPI_MIGRATION.md also ship. No `.dockerignore` sits beside the api-gateway Dockerfile. * **Scope:** the author's mail already states "the line removes two name shapes only". The two shapes that actually sit on the demo host are covered, so this is not a regression. * **Possible follow-up:** an allow-list (`COPY docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml ./docs/openapi/`), or `.dockerignore` lines for these shapes. That would also keep them out of the build context and the builder layer (F2). * **Reproduce:** plant the files above, then run `docker build -f services/api-gateway/Dockerfile Blockchain/Dev`, then `docker run --rm --entrypoint ls -la /app/docs/openapi`. **F2 (Info, by design). The backups still enter the build context and the builder-stage layer.** * The rm runs in the `builder` stage. The final stage copies the post-rm directory (`COPY --from=builder /app/docs/openapi`, Dockerfile:71), so the final image is clean; the layer scan above shows 0 entries. * The files are still uploaded as build context, which matters for a remote `az acr build`. They also stay in the builder's `COPY docs/openapi/` cache layer on the build host, and in any `--target builder` image. * The .dockerignore route from F1 would close this too. **F3 (Low, robustness). A directory with a matching name breaks the build.** * **What:** I planted `docs/openapi/old.rollback-dir/` and built with the head's Dockerfile. * **Result:** `rm: './docs/openapi/old.rollback-dir' is a directory`, then `exit code: 1`. The build failed. * **Why it is Low:** it fails closed, and no such directory exists today. * **What does not fail:** a clean tree with no match. busybox `rm -f` on an unmatched literal glob gives rc 0, and the clean build passed. * **Possible fix:** `rm -rf`, or `find … -type f`. **Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `rollback-` 21 hits including KS-1823. `.pre-*` 1 hit (KS-1823); `old.rollback-dir` 0; `x.bak` 0; `rm -f ./docs/openapi` 0; `dockerignore` 14 hits, of which KS-1289 (Done) is the `tests` versus `__tests__` pattern, a different defect. KS-1826 and KS-1813 read whole: neither mentions backups or the Dockerfile. KS-1823's own pull request comment lists "any name shape other than the two" as not done. **Not measured by this filing:** nothing was built or run here; the table and the failing build are the gate's measurements on a local arm64 Docker daemon.

title: anchoring index.ts:980 comment cites makeFetchDocFromAnchorStore, retired in KS 1628 (comment-only fix after KS 1822 merges)
description:
**BLUF:** Comment-only. The block comment above `GET /api/anchors/document/:documentId` in anchoring `index.ts` says gateway callers handle a non-200 by resolving null, and cites `makeFetchDocFromAnchorStore` in `api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts`. That function is gone: api-gateway's `verification.ts` says the verify mock route beside it was retired in KS 1628. The comment cites code that no longer exists. `index.ts` is Seat A 17th's file for KS 1822, so a later seat fixes this after that pull request merges.

## What I read (develop d7ddfa1f6433)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts:979-981`: "Gateway callers already handle non-200 by resolving null (see makeFetchDocFromAnchorStore in api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts), so the verifier-portal flow is unaffected."
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:388-393`: the comment block says the `/api/documents/:id/verify` mock (verification-level enforcement, a three-tier lookup including an `anchor_store` fallback) was retired in KS 1628 because nothing called it, and that its honesty rules were ported to originate first.
* `git grep` of every tracked file at develop d7ddfa1f6433: `makeFetchDocFromAnchorStore` has 2 hits, the comment above and `Blockchain/Dev/DEVELOPMENT.md:121` (the struck-through H2 row, which says the gateway's function "already handles non-200 by resolving null"). `api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` has 0. Controls in the same run: a symbol with known sites was found, a nonsense token found 0.
* Pull request 1813 (Seat A 17th, Refs KS 1822) is titled as making a foreign tenant's anchor read as absent on the two anchor GETs, so what callers do with a 404 from this route is exactly the claim the comment makes.

## What I did not read

* Whether any current gateway caller of the anchoring document route treats a non-200 as "no anchor". The comment's claim rests on the retired function, and nothing I read shows another caller does.
* The edit itself: it is a comment, in Seat A 17th's file, so I made none. The tracked-file grep above is the whole repo, so a later seat can reuse it.

## Source and searches

Wednesday's addendum, item E5 (the former item D of the Seat R 63rd brief). Board search (archived included, 2026-10-29 UTC, controls fired): "makeFetchDocFromAnchorStore" 4 hits (KS 1072, KS 1071, KS 1123, KS 1199), all about the function while it existed; none mentions this comment or the retirement. The line number was read at develop d7ddfa1f6433 and will move when KS 1822 merges.
